_about: Freshman batch 3: HS_102, 103, 104, 106, 107, 110 (all freshman season, no requirements). Every flag in each entry's _info.must_set_flags must be set by some choice (one per choice is pre-filled). Chain openers: HS_103 defended_teammate_online -> HS_139; HS_104 prioritized_family_trip / balanced_family_commitments -> HS_157; HS_106 trained_backup_holder -> HS_145; HS_107 community_volunteer -> HS_134.
_how: Fill in category, text and choices; leave _info alone (it's read-only). See tools/authoring/WRITING_GUIDE.md. Import: python3 tools/import_scenarios.py <this file> --dry-run

scenarios.title: The Open Gym
scenarios.text: The school opens the gym after classes, and a few players are setting up a kicking station. You have time to join them, but you also have homework and a chance to take the afternoon easy.

choices.label: Join the kicking session
choices.result: You take turns kicking into the practice net and get pointers on your approach. The extra reps sharpen your routine, though you get home later than planned.

choices.label: Save the afternoon
choices.result: You head home instead and get your assignments finished before relaxing. Your legs feel fresh the next day, but you miss a chance to get extra work in.

scenarios.title: The First Group Chat
scenarios.text: A group chat starts making fun of a teammate after an awkward moment at practice, and the jokes keep piling up. You know the teammate will probably see the messages, and everyone in the chat can see what you do next.

choices.label: Tell them to knock it off
choices.result: You say the jokes have gone too far and ask the group to leave the teammate alone. A few people go quiet, but you feel better knowing you didn't let it slide.

choices.label: Check in privately
choices.result: You message the teammate directly and let them know you saw the chat and don't agree with it. They appreciate hearing from you, even though the group chat carries on without you stepping in publicly.

choices.label: Join in with the jokes
choices.result: You add a joke of your own, and the chat fills with laughing reactions. It feels easy to fit in for the moment, but the teammate stops talking when you see them at practice.

scenarios.title: The Family Road Trip
scenarios.text: Your family has planned a road trip for the same weekend as your first kicking clinic. {parent} says the trip matters to everyone, while the clinic could give you a chance to learn from experienced kickers.

choices.label: Take the family trip
choices.result: You go on the trip and enjoy having everyone together without thinking about practice for a couple of days. You miss the clinic, but {parent} appreciates that you made the family plans a priority.

choices.label: Attend the kicking clinic
choices.result: You explain why the clinic matters and travel there while your family heads out. You get valuable instruction and several focused reps, though you miss the shared trip and {parent} is disappointed.

choices.label: Work out a split weekend
choices.result: You attend part of the clinic, then meet your family for the rest of the trip. You don't get the full clinic experience, but you still learn a few things and make time for everyone.

scenarios.title: The Substitute Holder

leads_to: unlocks HS_145 (The Holder's Big Moment) when trained_backup_holder

scenarios.text: Your usual holder, {holder}, is unavailable for part of practice, and a backup is filling in. The backup is still learning how to place the ball and time the snap, so you can either help them get comfortable or stick to your own routine.

choices.label: Help train the backup holder
choices.result: You slow things down and work through the snap, spot, and timing together. It takes time away from your own kicks, but the backup starts getting the ball down more consistently.

choices.label: Stick with your own routine
choices.result: You ask to keep your reps moving and let the coaches handle the backup's instruction. You get more kicks in, but the backup is still unsure about the timing when practice ends.

scenarios.title: The First Volunteer Day

leads_to: unlocks HS_134 (The Community Recognition) when community_volunteer

scenarios.text: A community volunteer day is coming up, and organizers need help setting up a youth sports field before the weekend games. You can commit to the full morning or stop by for a shorter shift around your other plans.

choices.label: Commit to the full morning
choices.result: All morning you're moving equipment, setting up cones, and getting the field ready. You're worn out by the end, but the organizers are grateful you stayed until the work was done.

choices.label: Help for a shorter shift
choices.result: You arrive early, help unload supplies, and stay until the main setup is finished. You have time for the rest of your day, though you leave before the final cleanup.

scenarios.title: The First Time You're Recognized
scenarios.text: After a kick that gets the sideline cheering, a school photographer asks for a quick picture and a few words about it. Teammates nearby are still celebrating, and you have to decide how to handle the attention.

choices.label: Give the team the credit
choices.result: You mention the snap, the hold, and the teammates who helped you prepare. The photographer gets a good quote, and your teammates appreciate that you included them in the moment.

choices.label: Enjoy the attention
choices.result: You smile for the camera and talk about how much the kick means to you. The attention feels great, though a couple of teammates think you could have mentioned the work everyone put in.

choices.label: Keep it low-key
choices.result: It was just one kick, you tell the photographer, and that there's plenty of work left to do. You avoid the spotlight, but some classmates read your answer as brushing off a moment they were excited to celebrate.
